config.note: Test 2: the joined draft sent whole in every call, as one window.

findings.note: "Review" is an action noun whose verb is carried by "conduct". The clause's main verb does the work of "review" instead.
"Realization" names the act of realizing, buried behind "had come to." The verb does little work.
"made" is an empty verb carrying the noun "decision", which buries the action of deciding.
"decision" is an action noun carried by the empty verb "was made"; the act of deciding is buried in the noun.
"evaluation" is an action noun carried by the empty verb "carried out"; the act of evaluating is buried in the noun.
"Undertaking" names the act of undertaking, and the clause's verb "has given" carries no meaning of its own.
"Assessment" names the act that "assess" expresses as a verb, and "carry out" does the clause's work instead.
"determination" is an action noun buried under "makes"; the verb "determine" is hidden. One buried verb carried by an empty verb.
The action "determine" is buried in the noun "determination", and the main verb is the empty "made" in the passive.
The action "meet" is buried in the noun "meeting", carried by "conducted" in the passive; no actor appears.
"Decision" carries the action while "made" does the verb work; the deciding subject is absent.
"expectation" is an action noun carried by "was", and the people doing the expecting never appear.
"resolution" names the act of resolving, and it is the subject of the empty verb phrase "would be arrived at" rather than of a verb like resolve.
"resolution" carries the action while "was arrived at" supplies only the tense, and no one resolves anything in the clause.
"observation" is the action of observing, buried under the empty verb "made".
The clause hides who is to do the noting; the draft never names that person.
The draft does not say who raised the concerns, so the source of a claim central to the argument is unnamed.

findings.quote: It was decided in 2023 that all changes would go through this process
findings.note: The clause never names who decided that all changes would go through this process. The surrounding sentences name only the board's recurring actions, not the actor behind this decision.
The draft does not say who conducted the meeting. Responsibility for how it was run is left unassigned.

findings.quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued
findings.note: The draft never says who was responsible for issuing flood warnings. The failure to issue them is the cost the paragraph is about.
No actor is named for the promise, and the surrounding sentences do not supply one. The paragraph faults an unnamed party for the sandbags that never arrived.

findings.quote: By the time I reached the top of the hill that February,
findings.note: The main subject "I" arrives after fifteen words of introductory clause.

findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus,
findings.note: The subject "I" arrives after 13 words of introductory phrase and clause.

findings.quote: At a quarter past four on the ninth of March,
findings.note: Thirteen words precede the main subject "Ellen Morrow".

findings.quote: Given the results of the pilot and what both teams told us in the May retrospective,
findings.note: Twenty words come before the subject "I", a subordinate clause before the main clause.

findings.quote: In the weeks after the water went down and the loss adjuster had come round to photograph each and every room,
findings.note: Twenty-three words precede the main subject "Ellen".
Three consecutive sentences open with the same two words, "Both ", followed by a different verb each time.

Personification of the cold as something that argues. The draft never establishes what the cold is arguing or to whom, so the figure supplies no mechanism beyond the literal claim that the cold no longer bothered the narrator.

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: Stock image standing in for the argument. The draft never develops what the toll does or who pays it, so the figure carries the claim on its own.
Stock image in a mixed figure with the paired safety-net image; the two cannot both hold, and the draft never states what the constraint actually is.

findings.quote: the beating heart of Quay Street
findings.note: Stock image. The draft never says what the bakery does for the street that a plain claim about its importance would not.

findings.quote: when a heart stops, the whole body feels it
findings.note: Mixed figure. The bakery-as-heart image is extended into a stopped heart and a feeling body, then abandoned in the next sentence.

findings.quote: A wave of support followed that lit a fire under the council
findings.note: Mixed figure. A wave and a fire are two incompatible images in one clause, and neither names what the support actually was.
Live figure: wording is figured as contraband crossing a border, but the app has no border in it. The mechanism behind the comparison is left unsaid.

Empty figure. The image supplies a picture of comfort and enclosure, but the draft never develops what the enclosure consisted of or what it shut out, so the comparison carries no mechanism beyond the adjective.

findings.quote: an anchor that kept me moored
findings.note: Mixed figure. A cocoon and an anchor cannot both describe the same car in the same sentence; one image is a container, the other a tether, and they pull in incompatible directions.
Empty figure. The simile asserts disclosure without indicating what is disclosed or how walking produces it; the literal claim would carry the same information.
Empty figure. The spatial image of landing supplies no picture the literal claim about the schema and preamble does not already carry.
Stock image standing in for an argument the paragraph does not make; nothing in the sentence explains what the street was meant to wake up to.
The summoning figure carried over from "a wake-up call" cannot hold in the same breath, since a call is answered by a person rather than by relocating flour.
"week" repeats within two sentences; the first occurrence is in "a week after my mechanic quoted me".
"picturesque" appears twice in one sentence, the second time in "the picturesque old mill"; the first is in "a picturesque row of Victorian houses".

findings.quote: I bought a new bike and a new lock
findings.note: "bike" appears in the preceding sentence ("My bike was stolen in June") and again here in the same sentence as "bike and a new lock"; "new" also repeats within the phrase.
"plain and simple" is a doubled pair saying one thing twice; "plain" and "simple" carry the same sense here.
Doubled pair: "full and complete" says one thing twice.
"cumbersome" appears twice within two sentences; the first occurrence is in "Its checklist is cumbersome for a one-line fix."

findings.quote: I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived at my desk with wet socks and a temper.
findings.note: Three consecutive sentences open with the same subject-verb template ("I left", "I reached", "I arrived"), adding nothing but sequence.
"Sodden" repeats from the previous sentence, where it appears in "the smell of sodden flour". The word does no new work in the second use.
"resolution was arrived at" repeats the preceding clause's wording within one sentence; the first occurrence is in "a resolution would be arrived at".
"decided" and "a decision" are the same root twice within one sentence. The nominalization also doubles the verb phrase "decided" / "would be made".

findings.quote: It is a feeling that recurs
findings.note: "feeling" appears in each of the last three sentences, with the first occurrence in "the feeling that nothing had been accomplished."

findings.quote: It is a feeling that is familiar. It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: "It is a feeling" opens two consecutive sentences built on the same template, following the earlier "with the feeling" in the first sentence.

findings.quote: no assessment, no strengths, no summary
findings.note: Three negative "no X" clauses in a row built on the same template. The pattern opens the sentence with "The schema has no".
"hall" appears twice within two sentences; the first is in "a borrowed kitchen at the community hall".
Doubled pair: "each and every" says one thing twice.
"LiveView" appears twice within two sentences; the first occurrence is in the preceding sentence, "Phoenix LiveView + elixir-desktop".

"She" opens four consecutive sentences, and the verb-in-second-position template repeats across all four. The same subject-first, past-tense-verb-second pattern appears in "She rang", "She carried", "She went" and "She left".
"major" echoes "major" in the preceding sentence ("Marking a revision major").
"null" appears in three of the four sentences here, following the earlier "nullable" in the first sentence, where the same root occurs.
"dialogs" repeats the word from the sentence before, which already used the same root in "system open and save dialogs".
"stale" appears twice within two sentences, the second time in the clause "stale is set by anchoring".
"Both" opens three consecutive sentences ("Both return", "Both filter", "Both start"), the same template running across the whole paragraph.
